comparison: Both evaluate claims C31-C41 about dLS neuron activation producing analgesia. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with converging gain/loss-of-function experiments. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, citing concerns about non-specific manipulation (need for c-Fos targeting) and questioning whether stress versus struggling drives analgesia.

Both evaluate claims C42-C49 about dLS neural activity specificity during restraint. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED though notes speculation about 'need to escape' interpretation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, directly challenging whether activity reflects stress versus intense struggling/motor behavior.

Both evaluate dLS→LHA pathway (C50-C56, C62-C63). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong anatomical and functional evidence. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, with editor noting 'convincing evidence' for the circuit, though Reviewer 1 asks about LHA specificity. Peer result also includes C2-C4 and C61 not in OpenEval result.

Both evaluate claims C57-C60 about opposite behavioral effects of activating dLS versus LHA neurons. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on logical inference from inhibitory connectivity. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting the bidirectional manipulation evidence without specific challenges.

Both evaluate claims C64-C69 about anatomical connectivity between inhibitory dLS and excitatory LHA neurons. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with multiple converging methods. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, noting cutting-edge techniques and accepting the anatomical characterization.

Both evaluate claims C70-C76 about temporal dynamics of dLS and LHA activity during struggle. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED though notes interpretation of subsequent inhibition is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED without specific challenges to the temporal dynamics findings.

Both address trisynaptic pathway anatomy (C77, C89-C91). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong anatomical evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning opioid system focus versus cannabinoid involvement and asking about direct LHA→RVM projections. Peer result includes additional claims C5-C6, C82-C85 about opioid mechanisms and RVM anatomy.

Both evaluate RVM neuron characterization (C92-C99) and coordinated circuit activity (C100-C101). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong temporal and behavioral evidence. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, noting convincing evidence, though Reviewer 3's stress versus struggle concern applies to overall interpretation.

Both evaluate claims C102-C106 about RVM neuron functional role through bidirectional manipulation. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with consistent opposite effects and pathway specificity. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting the bidirectional manipulation evidence without specific challenges.

Both evaluate claims C110-C112 about excitatory nature of RVM neurons. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with functional and anatomical evidence. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting the anatomical characterization as part of circuit identification.

Both evaluate mechanistic model claims (C100-C101, C113-C115). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as main mechanistic conclusion with coordinated activity evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 challenging stress versus struggle interpretation and Reviewer 1 requesting additional specificity validation.

Both evaluate opioid-dependence claims (C5, C80-C82). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with naltrexone blocking experiments. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning why authors focused on opioid system and noting critical role of endocannabinoid system, suggesting mechanism may be incomplete.

Partial overlap on RVM anatomical claims (C83-C85). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED for anatomical characterization and proposed mechanisms. Peer result R7 includes these claims but focuses more on opioid system questions and LHA→RVM connectivity uncertainty. Peer reviewers question completeness of opioid-only focus.

Minimal overlap on C33 (TetTox silencing reduces analgesia). OpenEval R1 evaluates this as part of comprehensive dLS manipulation evidence (SUPPORTED). Peer R12 specifically questions bidirectional evidence for stress-induced anxiety behaviors, rating UNCERTAIN and requesting clarification of stress/anxiety relationship to analgesia.

OpenEval R14 evaluates background/literature claims (C1, C10-C30) as SUPPORTED, noting they are appropriately cited prior knowledge providing context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval R15 evaluates additional literature claims (C78-C79, C107-C109) as SUPPORTED, noting they provide important context from prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
